title: Multi-model routing canary playbook and dataflow safety (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft documents an operational playbook for running canaries and small A/B exposures when routing across multiple model variants or model families (e.g., large base model -> distilled quantized variant -> reranker). It focuses on the intersection of routing decisions, dataflow (input/output transformations and sidecars), and safety/gating so cross-functional teams (prod, infra, model-ops, SRE, security) can coordinate predictable rollouts.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies when a single API route may be served by multiple model variants or when routing logic dynamically chooses model based on cost/latency/policy.
- Includes feature toggles, traffic slices, synthetic traffic stress, metric gating, and rollback recipes.
- Assumes Redwood runtime supports per-route routing policies and telemetry hooks; this playbook ties those primitives into a ceremony.

High-level rollout phases:
1) Preparation (owners assigned, hypothesis, quick smoke):
   - Owner: Product manager + Solutions-eng lead (default).
   - Define hypothesis: e.g., "quantized-ks-2 model offers 30% cost savings for short prompts with <5% degrade in nDCG on reranker set."
   - Identify critical slices (login & search queries, long-context workflows, embeddings batch jobs).
   - Baseline collection: 48–72h token-level latency/cost & quality snapshots on current default route.
   - Quick smoke tests in staging: zero-rate-limited runs, sample prompts across slices.

2) Canary design (tiny exposure, synthetic & live):
   - Canary size: start at 0.1% of requests or 1 request/min per slice for low-traffic products. For heavy routing functions, prefer fixed-requests-per-minute slice (example: 2rpm per microcohort).
   - Multi-dim slices: by locale, device type, feature flag state, and user tier.
   - Synthetic traffic harness: recorded golden inputs + adversarial probes to exercise edge cases (HTML payloads, truncated messages, long context).
   - Observability hooks: ensure route-level traces, token-level timing, and per-request model_id tag emitted to logs.

3) Monitor & guardrail gating (real-time + retrospective):
   - Real-time thresholds (automatic gate triggers):
     * 95th percentile token latency increase > 200ms relative to baseline AND > +20% at model-level -> pause exposure.
     * Error rate (5xx, inference timeouts) increase > 2x baseline OR absolute > 0.5% -> immediate rollback.
     * Cost per 1k tokens decreases < 5% but quality metric drops > 4% -> hold and escalate.
   - Quality signals (near-real-time):
     * Reranker/NLG fidelity measured with small in-band eval prompts (1 per 200 requests) and offline continuous evals every hour on a holdout prompt set.
     * Human-reviews: a tiny sample (10/day) from microcohorts for safety-sensitive routes.
   - Telemetry dashboards: per-model cost, per-model latency histogram, functional correctness (rerank precision/recall), and safety classifier score distribution.

4) Scale-up (progressive increased exposure):
   - Proposed increment cadence: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 4–24h stabilization windows depending on risk profile.
   - Safety gates must pass at each step. If a gate trips, perform root-cause checks and either roll back or run a targeted sweep (e.g., increased synthetic probes).

5) Post-decision (post-mortem / commit):
   - If fully rolled, capture metrics pre/post and update rollout policy to make variant default when appropriate.
   - If rolled back, populate incident ticket with timeline, traces, and minimum reproducible test.

Roles & responsibilities matrix (quick):
- Release owner (Product/Solutions): overall launch decision and stakeholder comms.
- Model-ops/Applied ML: model variant readiness, offline evals, adversarial tests.
- Infra/SRE: capacity and latency runbooks, throttle policies, autoscale knobs.
- Observability/Telemetry: dashboard ownership and alert tuning.
- Security/Trust: safety classifier thresholds and manual review queue.

Operational checklists (pre-canary):
- [ ] Model binary validated for same-API compatibility (tokenization, eos handling).
- [ ] KV cache behavior validated for warmed/unwarmed scenarios (no cache key collisions across variants).
- [ ] Fallthrough policy configured: e.g., fallback to default model variant on timeout or OOM.
- [ ] Rate-limits and quotas tested for canary traffic (ensure no global throttle bleed).
- [ ] Synthetic harness prepared and smoke inputs reviewed by product.

Canary observability runbook (what to check first 30m):
1) Latency: p50/p95/p99 vs baseline and per-model stream profile.
2) Error types: OOM, kernel assertion, grpc disconnects.
3) Output divergence: automated prompt-level similarity scores and rerank metric delta.
4) Downstream errors: client timeouts, UI thrash, odd user sessions.
5) Billing anomalies: per-minute cost spike on variant.

Rollback recipes (quick actions):
- Soft pause: reduce canary slice to 0% (route-level flag) and keep artifact for forensics.
- Hard rollback: revert route mapping to previous model_id, invalidate new model's cache entries, run a synthetic sweep on default.
- Emergency mute: disable non-essential downstream transforms to isolate where the failure lies (e.g., remove personalization features).

Failure-mode catalog (high-level):
- Performance regression on long context: symptom = p99 latency growth with stable p50, likely cause = KV-cache thrash or attention kernel mismatch. Remediation = limit max context for variant or lock to quantization profile with verified kernels.
- Semantic drift in niche slices: symptom = high divergence in reranker order for a particular cohort. Remediation = reduce exposure for cohort; add slice-specific weights to routing policy.
- Silent errors (bad tokens): symptom = subtle hallucination increase with safety classifier sliding but not tripping. Remediation = raise sampling of human review and refine in-band safety prompts.

Templates and scripts (examples):
- Canary creation CLI (example):
  rwdctl rollout create --route /generate --variant v2-q4 --slice "percent=0.1,cohort=search_internal" --monitoring "canary-v2-q4" --owner aisha.k
- Pause command:
  rwdctl rollout update --id <canary-id> --slice "percent=0" --reason "auto-pause:latency-trip"
- Synthetic run (local harness):
  python infra/tests/synthetic_harness.py --model v2-q4 --inputs samples/canary-golden.json --assertions metrics/expected_smoke.json

Communication and escalation (who to call):
- T+0–30m: notify rollout channel, Pager on-call SRE if p99 > threshold or >0.5% error rate.
- T+30–120m: joint triage meeting: Product, Model-ops, SRE, Observability. Capture decision to roll forward/rollback.
- Post-incident: 72h postmortem with remediation plan and test updates.

Safety knobs and permanent controls recommended:
- Route-level conservative default: always include a fast-fallback mapping that activates on any unknown failure.
- Per-cohort max exposure: policy that limits any single new variant to <5% of traffic for the first 30 days.
- Continuous small-sample evals: inject 1 in 200 requests a known-check prompt to keep signal on fidelity.

Open questions & follow-ups (to resolve before first cross-team roll):
- Where should we store golden prompt sets per-product (Confluence vs artifacts bucket)?
- What exact tagging schema will guarantee traceability across routing + model_id + quantization metadata?
- Do we want automated canary shrink on cost anomaly (cost increase despite latency improvement)?

Appendix: quick checklist for low-risk vs high-risk routes:
- Low-risk (internal tooling, non-user-facing): start 1% -> 10% -> 100% over 2–3h windows.
- Medium-risk (core search, feed): start 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% over 12h windows with human-review enabled.
- High-risk (financial, legal text generation): start with synthetic only + human-in-the-loop, no auto-scale beyond 0.5% until manual sign-off.

Notes and provenance:
This doc synthesizes runbook patterns observed in past Redwood rollouts and lessons from cross-team incidents. It is intentionally operational and prescriptive, meant to be adapted per product.

Last edits: 2026-02-10 by Aisha Khan (updated gating thresholds and added CLI examples).
